actions-list.actionItem: The House adjourned pursuant to a previous special order. The next meeting is scheduled for 9:00 a.m. on November 19, 2026.
On motion to adjourn Agreed to by voice vote.
Mr. Blair moved that the House do now adjourn.
The House resumed Special Order speeches.
The House received a message from the Senate. The Senate passed H.R. 5254 and H.R. 8454. Senate agreed to S. Res. 959.
The House has concluded all anticipated legislative business and has proceeded to Special Order speeches.
The House proceeded with further one minute speeches.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 7934.
Considered under suspension of the rules.
Mr. Palmer moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill. H.R. 7934 — "To amend chapter 3 of title 5, United States Code, to require the publication of settlement agreements, and for other purposes."

At the conclusion of debate, the Yeas and Nays were demanded and ordered. Pursuant to the provisions of clause 8, rule XX, the Chair announced that further proceedings on the motion would be postponed.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 4464.
Considered under suspension of the rules.
Mr. Arrington moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill. H.R. 4464 — "To amend the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 respecting the scoring of preventive health savings."
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by voice vote.
The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 5490.
Considered under suspension of the rules.

Mr. Mast moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended. H.R. 5490 — "To establish an interagency Task Force to dismantle and shut down transnational criminal syndicates perpetuating mass online scam operations against Americans."
The Speaker announced that votes on suspensions, if ordered, will be postponed until a time to be announced.
Mr. Mast asked unanimous consent that when the House adjourns today, it adjourn to meet at 9:00 a.m. on November 19. Agreed to without objection.
The House convened, returning from a recess continuing the legislative day of November 18.
The Speaker announced that the House do now recess. The next meeting is subject to the call of the Chair.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.

actions-list.header: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 396
actions-list.actionItem: 14 (Roll no. 326).
Considered as unfinished business. H.R. 9640 — "To amend the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act to reauthorize the Earth Mapping Resources Initiative, and for other purposes."
The House proceeded with one minute speeches, which by direction of the Chair would be limited to 15 per side of the aisle.
The Chair designated Mr. Kennedy of UT to lead the Members in reciting the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.
The Speaker announced approval of the Journal.  Pursuant to clause 1, rule I, the Journal stands approved.
Today's prayer was offered by the House Chaplain, Chaplain Margaret Grun Kibben.
The House convened, returning from a recess continuing the legislative day of November 18.
The Speaker announced that the House do now recess. The next meeting is scheduled for 12:00 P.M. today.
The House proceeded with Morning-Hour Debate. At the conclusion of Morning-Hour, the House will recess until 12:00 p.m. for the start of legislative business.
The Speaker designated the Honorable Ralph Norman to act as Speaker pro tempore for today.
The House convened, starting a new legislative day.
